_doc: THE CONDUCTOR'S / PRESENTATION VIEW — how the electronics are hinted at, section by section (decibel PLAN 2.7; RUNNING_LOG §320; DEC-99: 'not showing ensemble the returns, maybe a generic hint for conductor/presentation score, lets discuss, with visual options … section by section'). `sections`: the piece's sections in order — `does` is what the electronics do there, in plain words; a section with `options` is the one in hand: its `window` (seconds of the piece, one page of 12) and the ways of hinting, each a `kind` the builder knows (echoTriangles · band · echoArcs · lane · none). A section's `chosen` (an option's id) when he has said. tools/signs/build_conductor.js draws the page from the piece's own save.

sections.name: 1 · The opening (0 … 37 s)
sections.does: Each player's short attack is recorded. From the second round on, every new attack is shadowed by that player's EARLIER attacks, transformed: first one of them, then two, three, four, five. They fall a little before, around or after the live note, never exactly with it, and the engine rolls their exact times at each performance.
sections.windowNote: Its second page: here the returns grow from one sound to two, then three.

options.name: echo triangles
options.what: One small grey open triangle for each returning sound, set loosely across the stretch they come back in.
options.for: The short attacks' own sign, greyed: it reads as "that attack, echoed". You see the count grow from one to five.

options.name: a pale bar
options.what: A pale bar at the bottom of the lane over the stretch, with a dot for each returning sound.
options.for: Closest to the composer score's own return brick. Exact about the stretch; says nothing false about when each sound falls inside it.

options.name: echo arcs
options.what: Sound-wave arcs just after the attack, one for each returning sound.
options.for: The most compact, and the most generic: "this attack echoes, this many times". It takes almost no room in the lane.

options.name: a lane of its own
options.what: A thin sixth lane under the five. A bar for each return, on the row of the player whose sound it is.
options.for: The five lanes stay exactly as the players see them: the conductor's score is the players' score plus one strip. The lanes each lose a few pixels of height.

options.name: nothing drawn
options.what: The page as the players see it. The performance notes say what the electronics do.
options.for: The cleanest. A conductor learns the section's behaviour once, from the notes.

sections.held: HELD at his word 2026-10-09 (DEC-100). His idea: the FLOCKING badge and some sort of duration line or line wedge over the stretch, marked as ELECTRONICS behaviour by a constant difference — its place in the lane, its size, a transparency or a colour, an italics equivalent. The five options below were drawn before he said it (RUNNING_LOG §320).

sections.name: 2 · The three body problem (39 … 123 s)
sections.does: Three computer players join the five. They move through the same four states as the players — far apart, approaching, close pass, break and rejoin — listen to them, and decide each sound live, from the transformed attacks.

sections.name: 3 · Trills and petal hits (125 … 210 s)
sections.does: At the end of each trill another player plays one short note into an open microphone, and the electronics ring it on as a long resonant tail of about ten seconds. Thirty-four of them.

sections.name: 4 · The drones (211 … 415 s)
sections.does: Each player's held multiphonic is recorded three times. Each recording comes back stretched into drones of 10 to 40 seconds, up to five at once, until a long fade at the end.

sections.name: 5 · The beating section (423 … 668 s)
sections.does: The electronics hold a pure tone at the player's pitch. The player bends against it, so the pair beats. Thirty-five pairs.

sections.name: 6 · The strikes (not yet in the piece)
sections.does: The ensemble strikes. The electronics answer after the strike, with its rhythm transformed, on the recorded attacks.
